stem:
Meena's mother cooks spinach for dinner. After cooking, Meena notices that the spinach has lost its bright green colour and become soft. Her grandmother says that cooking can also reduce some nutrients in vegetables.

Which statement correctly explains what happens when vegetables are cooked?

options.text: Cooking destroys all the nutrients in vegetables, so cooked vegetables have no nutritional value.
Cooking can change the colour and texture of vegetables and may reduce some nutrients such as vitamin C, while other nutrients remain.
Cooking has no effect on vegetables, so raw and cooked vegetables always contain exactly the same nutrients.
Cooking increases the amount of vitamin C in vegetables because heat adds nutrients to the food.

teacher.key_rationale: Cooking can alter colour and texture and can reduce heat-sensitive nutrients like vitamin C, but it neither destroys all nutrients nor leaves everything unchanged, so B is the only accurate statement. A overstates (all nutrients destroyed), C understates (no change), D reverses the direction (heat adds vitamin C).
